purpose: Additional questions fixed before their first paid evaluation; answer-key references never enter ordinary retrieval.

questions: Under the 2022 NYC Building Code, what is the required height range for a handrail along an ordinary office stair, and where is it measured from?
For that ordinary stair, is a handrail uniformly 39 inches above the tread nosings acceptable along the flight? This is not a transition fitting.
Correction: the handrail is uniformly 36 inches above the tread nosings. Does it satisfy that height range, without deciding other stair requirements?
checks: 34 to 38 inches above tread nosings; ordinary stair distinguished from special devices
39 exceeds ordinary maximum; no transition-fitting exception

questions: Under the 2022 NYC Plumbing Code, are S-traps permitted for ordinary plumbing fixtures?
Could I use a drum trap instead for an ordinary lavatory? This is not a solids interceptor or chemical waste system.
For a separate hypothetical chemical waste system, does the drum-trap prohibition have an exception?
checks: Drum trap prohibited in specified ordinary use
Drum traps serving chemical waste systems permitted by specific exception; no blanket installation approval

questions: Under the 2022 NYC Mechanical Code, how far must an outdoor air intake for a Group B building on a 40-foot-wide lot be from the side lot line? It does not face a street or public way.
For that same case, would an intake 8 feet from the side lot line meet the lot-line separation requirement?
Now consider a separate Group B building on an 18-foot-wide lot. What does the narrow-lot provision say about the intake location between the side lot lines?
checks: 10 feet from side lot line; narrow-lot and R-3 exceptions do not apply to described case
Less-than-20-foot lot provision requires centerline between lot lines; not blanket full compliance

questions: Under the 2022 NYC Fuel Gas Code, can a gas appliance be installed in a bathroom? Explain the basic restriction and the direct-vent exception.
Would the same direct-vent exception allow installation in a bedroom used for sleeping?
Returning to the bathroom example: is calling the appliance direct-vent enough, or does that exception impose additional conditions?
checks: Bathroom generally prohibited; direct-vent exception only non-sleeping rooms with all combustion air outdoors and listing/manufacturer conditions
No; exception excludes rooms used for sleeping
All combustion air directly outdoors plus listing and manufacturer instructions; label alone insufficient

questions: Assume NYC ZR 37-34 applies to the primary frontage. If the ground-floor ceiling is 14 feet above a level adjoining sidewalk, what vertical band is used for the 50 percent transparency calculation?
For that same 14-foot ceiling, use an applicable wall 30 feet wide with no exempt openings. What are the measured wall area and required transparent area?
If I provide that total glazing area but leave one uninterrupted opaque wall segment 12 feet wide, is satisfying the area percentage alone enough under that section?
checks: From 2 to 14 feet above adjoining sidewalk because ceiling is higher than 12 feet
12-foot band times 30 feet = 360 square feet; at least 180 square feet transparent
No; uninterrupted opaque width maximum 10 feet, independent of total percentage
